high_consensus.description: This is a real spec gap with high downstream rework risk. Override/merge semantics are core to correctness, and leaving them undefined creates divergent implementations and operator surprises.
Strong operability improvement. Pre-flight validation alone is insufficient for runtime debugging in a precedence-based resolver; lightweight resolution traces materially improve supportability.
Critical startup behavior is underspecified. File-missing/parse/permission failures are common real-world conditions and must be explicitly fail-open/fail-closed defined.
Valuable hardening item. mtime-only invalidation and concurrent regeneration races are practical issues, though implementation complexity is moderate and may be staged after core semantics.
High-value, concrete compatibility safeguard. The PRD promises legacy support; enumerated fixtures and golden tests are the most direct way to prevent silent regressions.

blockers.concern: Endpoint allowlist security can be bypassed without strict canonicalization and DNS/IP revalidation
blockers.why_matters: Hostname allowlisting alone is fragile (IDN/punycode, redirects, DNS rebinding, IPv6 literals, mixed schemes/ports). SSRF protections may be incomplete under real-world resolver behavior.
blockers.recommendation: Specify canonical URL parser, enforce HTTPS + default ports, resolve-and-verify final IPs at request time, and deny redirects across trust boundaries.

blockers.concern: Permission-elevation rejection rule is underspecified for new operator-added models with no baseline entry
blockers.why_matters: If baseline permissions are missing, the system may either over-reject legitimate configs or accidentally allow permissive defaults. Both outcomes block adoption or create security exposure.
blockers.recommendation: Define deterministic policy: operator-added models default to minimal permissions unless explicitly approved in System Zone registry; reject otherwise with guided remediation.

blockers.concern: Release-blocking deferred decisions (DD-1..DD-5) are still unresolved, but Sprint 1 depends on them
blockers.why_matters: Core implementation paths (permissions source-of-truth, schema placement, override semantics, startup hook language, schema validator integration) cannot be built safely until these are fixed. This is a high-probability schedule slip and rework trigger.
blockers.location: Scope & Prioritization -> Deferred decisions to resolve before Sprint 1
blockers.recommendation: Add a pre-Sprint 1 decision milestone with owners, deadlines, and explicit fallback choices if consensus is not reached within 48-72 hours.

blockers.concern: Resolution logic is too complex for reliable correctness in v1 (6-stage precedence + legacy shapes + prefer_pro overlay + tier mappings)
blockers.why_matters: Even with FR-3.9, combinatorial interactions can produce misrouting that is hard to detect in production. A subtle precedence bug directly changes model selection behavior, cost, and output quality.
blockers.location: FR-3.7, FR-3.8, FR-3.9; Technical Considerations -> Backward-compat for legacy skill_models shapes
blockers.recommendation: Reduce initial state-space: disable one legacy shape per skill in v1 or gate prefer_pro overlay behind explicit opt-in for migrated skills only; add property-based tests for precedence invariants.

blockers.concern: Runtime-generated `.run/merged-model-aliases.sh` design does not define concurrency/atomicity guarantees
blockers.why_matters: Concurrent process starts can read partially written files or stale cache state, causing intermittent startup failures or inconsistent model maps across invocations.
blockers.recommendation: Require atomic write via temp file + rename, file locking, and monotonic version header checks before sourcing.
